about: Capture-time provenance for docs/screens/*.png (#335). One row per shot, written by the session that took the pixels: sha256/canvas are properties of the bytes, origin/install/url/seed/level/layout/sampleRate/build are properties of the instrument and cannot be recovered from the PNG afterwards. `node tools/recap.js check` verifies each row against the file it addresses and against every other row of the same (seed, level, sampleRate); the vocabulary, the route verdicts and the audio-draw rule live in tools/recap.js, not here.

4abba57.note: The four blobs that draw a frame, sha256, read from the checkout that ran the capture. index.html plus the three js/ files that put a pixel on screen: js/10_assets.js makes the textures, js/20_level.js the lit materials, js/40_render.js is the rasterizer. `node tools/recap.js check` recomputes them from the tree it runs in and prints whether these frames still show what that tree ships (#536). The session that took these pixels proved this build off the wire, blob by blob, against the deployed page.

39edaf3.note: The twelve blobs that build serves - index.html and every script its own index.html loads - as sha256, read from that build. `node tools/recap.js check` recomputes them from the tree it runs in and prints whether these frames still show what that tree ships (#536). This entry is a BIND RE-KEY, not a capture: the pixels were taken at b7a40d6 by the pass described in tools/recap.js and README.md, and #910 measured what main at 39edaf3 draws from the same route - all eight poses re-rendered off https://lioreshai.github.io/breach-protocol-flash-next/ after that deploy sha256-matched origin/main four for four. The frames came back with no world pixel moved: three of the eight are byte-identical to the committed bytes and the other five differ only inside the columns the held rig occupies (0.03% to 0.39% of the frame, every mean within 0.01 luma), which is the load-to-load disagreement #611 already names, not a surface being fetched differently. So the PNGs are carried and only the bind moves. The blob that moved is js/20_level.js, and what moved in it is a jump predicate (#893): a still frame cannot show it because the feet are on the ground.

f42f5ce.note: The 12 blobs that build serves - index.html and every script its own index.html loads - as sha256, read from that build, and proved off the wire before the shutter: for each of them the bytes served by https://lioreshai.github.io/breach-protocol-flash-next/ sha256-match `git show f42f5ce:<file>`, 12 for 12. `node tools/recap.js check` recomputes them from the tree it runs in and prints whether these frames still show what that tree ships (#536). This entry is a CAPTURE: the pixels in the rows that name it were taken from that page by the pass tools/livecap.js FRAMES describes.

shots.note: Re-taken off the deployed page at b5b8b74 for #916, the build the bind names: that page was proved blob by blob first - index.html and every script it loads, 12 in all, sha256-match `git show b5b8b74:<file>` 12 for 12 - and the shutter ran on that page afterwards, so these are the pixels the shipped bytes draw and not a harness render. Route: one page load and one boot per pose (js/90_dev.js refuses a second DEV.boot() in a load), the pose left where the deal put the seat, DEV.freeze(true), DEV.set("grain",0), DEV.clear() before the shutter, the display pinned to 1440x763 by livecap's --vp (this chromium reports innerHeight 620 for every --window-size), toDataURL handed back RGBA and the frame re-encoded to colour type 2 through tools/png_rgb.js. The dealt signature is the one the replaced row named (4083630493) and the audio term is carried rather than read: these headless loads have no output device, so SND.init never sets SND.ac and sampleRate is not readable off the page (#404); the control is that the term sets how many draws precede generation, so had it moved the signature would have moved with it, and it did not. What these bytes replace (rev b5b8b74, mean 60.5867, which bound f42f5ce) differs from them by 666 px (0.06%) of pixels under the kept-pixel rule and -0.0012 of mean luma; where they are is stated in the README caption this row addresses.
